Retrospective peels

Source: R/9-retro_and_jitter.R
retrospective.Rd

Refit an Rceattle model with its last 1, 2, ..., peels years of data removed, and calculate Mohn's rho for the terminal year and the nyrs_forecast years after it. Each peel is fitted twice: its hindcast, then F in the removed years, fitted to their observed catch with the hindcast held fixed.

Usage

retrospective(
  object = NULL,
  peels = 5,
  rescale = FALSE,
  nyrs_forecast = 3,
  cores = NULL,
  getsd = NULL,
  phase = TRUE,
  fit_control = NULL,
  projected_env_data_known = FALSE,
  Rceattle = NULL
)

Arguments

object

an Rceattle model fit using fit_mod().

peels

number of retrospective peels (default 5).

rescale

which env_data columns to standardize on each peel's retained years: FALSE (default) none, TRUE every numeric column except Year, random-effect grouping columns and columns a linkage reads as a category, or a character vector of column names.

nyrs_forecast

number of years after each peel's terminal year for which Mohn's rho is also calculated (default 3).

cores

Number of cores for the parallel refits. Default NULL picks parallel::detectCores() - 6, capped at 2 under R CMD check (which sets _R_CHECK_LIMIT_CORES_). Set to 1 to force sequential execution.

getsd

whether each peel reports standard errors; NULL (default) does so only if object holds an sdrep.

phase

whether each peel is refitted in phases (default TRUE); a peel starts from the unpeeled model's estimates.

fit_control

optional fit_control() bundle for the refits. Only phase and getsd are read; see What fit_control() reaches.

projected_env_data_known

env_data columns whose values after each peel's terminal year were known then, such as a climate projection, so the peels keep them (a categorical linkage term or a q or selectivity random effect keeps its terminal-year value regardless): FALSE (default) none, TRUE all, or a character vector of column names.

Rceattle

deprecated name for object, still accepted so existing scripts keep working. Supplying both is an error.

Value

An Rceattle_retro list:

Rceattle_list

each kept peel, deepest first, then the unpeeled model, named for its terminal year (e.g. Year_2016); index by name, since a dropped peel leaves a gap.

mohns

Mohn's rho, the mean over peels of (peel - unpeeled) / unpeeled, by Object (biomass, ssb, R, F_spp) and Forecast year (0 = the peel's terminal year), one column per species, with N the number of peels averaged (NaN where N is 0, with no warning unless no peel converged).

peels_requested

the peels asked for.

Details

Hindcast and forecast years. A peel's hindcast is the model as it would have been fitted at its terminal year: it ends there, so no later index, composition or catch, and no parameter for a later year, enters its estimates. It starts from the unpeeled estimates for its own years and uses the unpeeled map cut to them. Its removed years are then its retrospective forecast: F is fitted to the observed catch with the hindcast fixed at its estimates. Weight-at-age, empirical selectivity and ration stay at the terminal year, and the q and selectivity deviations keep their terminal-year values (a form whose deviations are year-to-year increments takes an increment of 0). M1 deviations take the peel's projection values: 0 for one estimated by year, an input series as given. A q or selectivity linkage random effect keeps its terminal-year level too, as the projection holds selectivity. Any other linkage effect takes the peel's own estimate for each removed year, as the projection does: a random walk its terminal value, an AR1 its decay toward 0, an IID effect 0. Recruitment takes the deviation sample_rec() uses with sample_rec = FALSE, computed from the peel's fit (for a penalty-form curve with no penalty years in the peel, the mean over its own years after the first). Each peel's data_list holds endyr and endyr_peel (its terminal year), endyr_full (the unpeeled terminal year, where the forecast ends) and projyr (the end of the projection). The forecast years are endyr_peel + seq_len(endyr_full - endyr_peel), which is empty for the unpeeled model, where (endyr_peel + 1):endyr_full would count down.

Dropped and flagged peels. A peel whose hindcast did not converge is dropped, with a warning; under getsd = TRUE that includes a hindcast Hessian that is not positive definite, as when a category level begins after the peel's terminal year and so leaves its estimated coefficient with no data (getsd = FALSE keeps that peel). A peel whose forecast refit did not fit F to the catch (gradient check, or a peeled F at a bound) is kept but left out of the $mohns rows with Forecast year above 0, and attr(peel, "forecast_refit_error") gives the reason. Check it before reading that peel's forecast years: only plot_timeseries() and its wrappers warn about them.

Standard errors. Mohn's rho reads only point estimates, so getsd = FALSE is faster. Under getsd = TRUE each peel is rebuilt at its estimates with the hindcast parameters treated as estimated, so no estimate moves. A fitted year's band is the peel's hindcast's own, except a depletion relative to last-projection-year biomass (HCR = "NoFishing", msmMode > 0, DynamicHCR = FALSE), which reads the peeled F. A forecast year's band treats the catch as known and carries the hindcast's uncertainty through the F needed to take it, without recruitment variability, so it is narrower than a prediction interval. If the rebuild fails (an error, or no finite standard error), the peel is kept, but plots, as.data.frame() and vcov() ignore its sdrep, which may not hold valid standard errors; attr(peel, "sd_report_error") gives the reason. print() counts the peels carrying either attribute; retrospective() warns about neither.

Environmental data. A peel's forecast should read only what was known at its terminal year, so after that year a peel treats each env_data column by how the model reads it:

  • an observed covariate (linkage_spec(observe = )) loses its observations;

  • a column the model reads directly (a Cindex temperature, an environmental catchability or M1) takes the retained years' mean, as in any missing year;

  • a numeric fixed-effect linkage covariate, a 0/1 block column included, takes the retained years' mean, with a warning; a term computed over the whole column, such as scale(), then changes in the retained years too;

  • a fixed-effect category, such as cut(Year, ...), factor(regime) or a logical column, holds its terminal-year value (linkage_spec()), though one cut from the whole column, such as cut(temp, 3), still sets its breaks from the whole column, post-peel years included;

  • a random-effect grouping column, a column with no retained value, and a fixed-effect covariate that is also observed, also read as a category (the category term is still held), or logical but read as a number (as.numeric(flag)) keep their post-peel values, with a warning; Mohn's rho is then conditional on them (a q or selectivity random effect takes its terminal-year level whatever its grouping column says);

  • a column listed in projected_env_data_known keeps its values with no warning, though a category is still held.

Refitting a returned peel's data_list with fit_mod() does not hold its categories, while its numeric covariates stay mean-filled; a diagnostic such as jitter() or profile() does not work on a returned peel.

rescale standardizes a column on the retained years and applies that centre and scale to the whole column (a column with fewer than two distinct retained values stays in its units, with a warning). Name the columns when env_data also holds an input that is not a covariate, such as a Cindex temperature in degrees C, which TRUE would turn into z-scores. The unpeeled model is not rescaled, so standardize those columns the same way before fitting it.

Catchability. A peel's hindcast uses the unpeeled model's map, cut to its years, so a survey whose index falls only in the removed years keeps a free q with no index to inform it, which under getsd = TRUE can leave the Hessian not positive definite and drop the peel.

Examples

# \donttest{
data(BS2017SS)
ss_run <- fit_mod(data_list = BS2017SS, inits = NULL, file = NULL,
                  estimateMode = 0, random_rec = FALSE, msmMode = 0,
                  fit_control = fit_control(phase = FALSE, verbose = 0))
#> `age_trans_matrix` data does not span range of age for species 1 will fill with 0s
retro <- retrospective(ss_run, peels = 10)
# }
